plan: Sell SOXL and SPAL to zero to eliminate all leveraged ETF exposure.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the single name mandate.
Add to QQQI, increasing its allocation to 25% to favor income and broad index exposure.
Buy META at 5% of the book, adding a top-quality name from the scanner.
This plan prioritizes capital preservation and a large cash buffer.
conservative.read: This conservative plan targets around 1.5% per month, focusing on capital preservation and low drawdown. It significantly reduces risk by eliminating leveraged ETFs and diversifying holdings. Expect steady, but modest, returns with tight stops.

plan: Trim SOXL to 3% and SPAL to 2% to reduce overall leveraged ETF exposure.
Trim SPY to 25% to meet the single name concentration mandate.
Buy META at 4% of the book, adding a strong scanner setup.
Trim QQQI to 15% to rebalance the portfolio towards growth.
This plan balances risk and growth with a moderate cash buffer.
balanced.read: This balanced plan targets around 2.5% per month, aiming for risk-first growth. It reduces leverage and concentration while blending broad index with quality tech. Expect moderate returns with controlled drawdown.

plan: Trim SPY to 25% to meet the single name concentration mandate.
Add to SOXL, increasing its allocation to 6%, leaning into semiconductors.
Add to SPAL, increasing its allocation to 6%, to increase leveraged exposure.
Buy META at 6% of the book, adding a highest-scoring scanner setup.
Add to CRWD, increasing its allocation to 18%, pressing what is working.
This plan uses leverage and concentration for stretch growth.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets around 4% per month, aiming for stretch growth by using leverage and concentrating in high-scoring setups. Be aware this raises both upside and drawdown significantly. Leveraged ETFs decay daily, and this mode can lose a lot fast; strict stop discipline is critical.

plan: Sell SOXL and SPAL to zero to eliminate all leveraged ETF exposure.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and rebalance the portfolio.
Add to QQQI, increasing its allocation to 30%, rotating into an income ETF.
Trim QQQ to 10% to reduce growth exposure and favor income.
This plan prioritizes steady monthly distributions and low drawdown.
income.read: This income plan targets around 1% per month, focusing on parking cash for yield and steady monthly distributions. It cuts leverage and high-beta names to near zero. Distributions are variable and NAV can still fall in a selloff; this is cash-like income, not a savings account.
